meta.chapterLabel: Lesson 5: Shopping (2): Two Bottles of That Wine, Please (Extras)
meta.baseChapterLabel: Lesson 5: Shopping (2): Two Bottles of That Wine, Please

items.english: Bag
items.target: ふくろ
items.pronunciation: fukuro
items.reviewNote: From the lesson VOCABULARY list. It is the only lesson-5 headword with no card at all, and the TARGET DIALOGUE's last line needs it. Its english 'Bag' collides with the existing Lesson 2 card かばん (kaban), so both need a hint — this one has one; かばん does not and should be given one.
items.note: This is the paper or plastic bag a shop puts your purchase in. The bag you carry your own things in is かばん (kaban), from Lesson 2.

items.english: How much is the red mug?
items.target: あかいマグカップはいくらですか
items.pronunciation: akai magukappu wa ikura desu ka
items.reviewNote: From EXERCISES 3, the worked example (verbatim). GRAMMAR 3 (adjective before noun) has exactly one card in the deck, the KS3 statement; this is the same grammar inside a question, and it puts the stranded マグカップ and あかい vocabulary to work. Its answer form is already covered by nisen-roppyaku-en-desu, so I did not add a second price answer.

items.english: I would like three cheesecakes and two apple pies, please.
items.target: チーズケーキをみっつとアップルパイをふたつください
items.pronunciation: chīzukēki o mittsu to appurupai o futatsu kudasai
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 2 (verbatim). This is the only sentence in the lesson that orders two different counted items in one breath, and it is the only thing that uses the stranded チーズケーキ and アップルパイ vocabulary cards. It also puts みっつ and ふたつ into a sentence — until now the つ-counters only existed as recitation cards plus the single それをむっつください drill.
items.note: Each item carries its own を (o) and its own counter, and と (to) joins the two orders. ください (kudasai) comes once, at the end.

items.english: Four towels, please.
items.target: タオルを４まいください
items.pronunciation: taoru o yon-mai kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed, but it is exactly the answer EXERCISES 7.2 asks the learner to produce (タオル, 4まい). Serves the VOCABULARY job for タオル and adds a second まい sentence — before wave 1 the deck had ten まい recitation cards and zero sentences.
items.ttsText: タオルをよんまいください

items.english: Three of those mikan oranges, please.
items.target: そのみかんをみっつください
items.pronunciation: sono mikan o mittsu kudasai
items.reviewNote: Lifted verbatim from EXERCISES 6, the worked example. Serves the FORM job (nounを number ください) and the VOCABULARY job — みかん sat in the deck as a bare noun with no sentence. Wave 1 did not take this one.

items.english: One of those large bags, please.
items.target: そのおおきいふくろを１まいください
items.pronunciation: sono ōkii fukuro o ichi-mai kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for おおきい, which had no sentence. Builds on wave 1's ふくろも２まいください rather than repeating it: singular いちまい instead of にまい, and a plain request instead of an 'as well' one.
items.note: Bags count with まい (mai) because they are flat when empty, the same counter as shirts and sheets of paper.
items.ttsText: そのおおきいふくろをいちまいください

items.english: This is an English bag.
items.target: これはイギリスのかばんです
items.pronunciation: kore wa igirisu no kaban desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job for の as the origin member of the minimal pair. イギリス is from Lesson 1.
items.note: The other half of the pair with これはわたしのかばんです (kore wa watashi no kaban desu). A place before の (no) says where the thing was made, never who it belongs to — this bag is not owned by England.

items.english: Is this black bag also 10,000 yen?
items.target: このくろいかばんも10,000えんですか
items.pronunciation: kono kuroi kaban mo ichiman'en desu ka
items.reviewNote: From EXERCISES 5, the worked example (verbatim). Exercise 5 produced no cards. No card in this lesson uses も, and this stacks この + adjective + noun in one question, which nothing else in the deck does.
items.ttsText: このくろいかばんもいちまんえんですか

items.english: How much is that large vacuum cleaner over there?
items.target: あのおおきいそうじきはいくらですか
items.pronunciation: ano ōkii sōjiki wa ikura desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for おおきい and puts そうじき to work outside its single どこですか card. GRAMMAR 3 (adjective before noun) had one worked example in the deck before wave 1 and two after; this is a third with a different adjective type — size rather than colour.

items.english: Apples are 100 yen.
items.target: りんごは100えんです
items.pronunciation: ringo wa hyaku-en desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job: は and も are the lesson's two topic-slot particles and the deck never shows them swapped in one otherwise identical sentence.
items.note: Half of a minimal pair with みかんも100えんです (mikan mo hyaku-en desu). は (wa) just names the topic and says nothing about anything else.
items.ttsText: りんごはひゃくえんです

items.english: These aren't Italian shoes.
items.target: これはイタリアのくつじゃありません
items.pronunciation: kore wa itaria no kutsu ja arimasen
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job as the negative rung, on the same noun as kore-wa-itaria-no-kutsu. Wave 1's スイスのじゃありません negates a noun-dropped のです; this one negates the full placeの noun phrase, which is the shape GRAMMAR 4 actually teaches.
items.note: Member 2 of the set. じゃありません (ja arimasen) from Lesson 2 simply replaces です (desu); nothing else in the sentence moves.

items.english: One beer and two bottles of wine, please.
items.target: ビールを１ぽんとワインを２ほんください
items.pronunciation: bīru o ip-pon to wain o ni-hon kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job. This is the only card anywhere that puts two forms of the same counter side by side, which is the fastest way to see that the change is driven by the number in front, not by the object.
items.note: One counter, two sounds in a single breath: いっぽん (ip-pon) after いち (ichi), にほん (ni-hon) after に (ni).
items.ttsText: ビールをいっぽんとワインをにほんください

items.english: Are the cameras on the fourth floor?
items.target: カメラは４かいですか
items.pronunciation: kamera wa yon-kai desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for よんかい and the FORM job — every location question in the deck uses どこ, so the yes/no version of GRAMMAR 1 had no example at all.
items.note: You can check a location without どこ (doko): name a floor and add か (ka).
items.ttsText: カメラはよんかいですか

items.english: Three beers, please.
items.target: ビールを３ぼんください
items.pronunciation: bīru o san-bon kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job — of the three counter shapes ほん／ぼん／ぽん, only ほん had ever appeared in a sentence (ks5-two-bottles-wine). Also the first sentence use of ビール as the thing being bought rather than asked about.
items.note: ほん (hon) softens to ぼん (bon) after さん (san). That is why the deck has three separate spellings of the same counter.
items.ttsText: ビールをさんぼんください

items.english: No, it isn't Swiss. It's French.
items.target: いいえ、スイスのじゃありません。フランスのです
items.pronunciation: īe, suisu no ja arimasen. furansu no desu
items.reviewNote: From EXERCISES 4A, the worked example (verbatim), paired with kore-wa-suisu-no-tokei-ka. This is the only place in the lesson where the placeの pattern is negated, and there is no card for it anywhere in the deck.
items.note: Correcting someone runs in two parts: deny with じゃありません (ja arimasen), then supply the right answer. じゃありません is from Lesson 2.
items.scene: answering whether the watch is Swiss

items.english: Please give me two bags as well.
items.target: ふくろも２まいください
items.pronunciation: fukuro mo ni-mai kudasai
items.reviewNote: From the TARGET DIALOGUE (verbatim). This is the highest-value missing card in the lesson: the deck has ten いちまい…じゅうまい recitation cards and not one sentence that uses まい. It also carries the も particle into a counted request.
items.note: Bags count with まい (mai) because they are flat, the same counter as shirts and sheets of paper. Bottles took ほん (hon) two lines earlier in the same dialogue.
items.ttsText: ふくろもにまいください

items.english: Yes, that one is Japanese too.
items.target: はい、それもにほんのです
items.pronunciation: hai, sore mo nihon no desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed, paired with ookii-kamera-mo-nihon-no-ka. Serves the PARTICLE job for も in an answer, and repeats the pointer switch that EXERCISES 5 singles out ('Change the pronoun to fit each item') on different material from wave 1's bag exchange.
items.note: The customer says その (sono) and the assistant answers それ (sore) — from behind the counter the same camera is now the near one.
items.scene: answering whether the large camera is also Japanese

items.english: It's 2,600 yen.
items.target: 2,600えんです
items.pronunciation: nisen roppyaku-en desu
items.reviewNote: From the TARGET DIALOGUE (verbatim), paired with ikura-desu-ka. The lesson has no price-answer card of its own; the nearest is 13,000えんです back in Lesson 4.
items.ttsText: にせんろっぴゃくえんです
items.scene: answering how much the wine costs

items.english: That camera is an American one.
items.target: そのカメラはアメリカのです
items.pronunciation: sono kamera wa amerika no desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job as the middle rung of the demonstrative ladder, on the same noun as kono-kamera-wa-nihon-no so the only thing that changes is the pointer.
items.note: Member 2 of the この (kono) / その (sono) / あの (ano) set. その is the thing nearer the person you are talking to.

items.english: Is that large camera also a Japanese one?
items.target: そのおおきいカメラもにほんのですか
items.pronunciation: sono ōkii kamera mo nihon no desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job for も — every other も card in the deck is about matching prices, so nothing showed it working on a country of origin. Also a third stacking of demonstrative plus adjective plus noun.

items.english: Where is the restroom?
items.target: おてあらいはどこですか
items.pronunciation: otearai wa doko desu ka
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 3 (verbatim). The deck already has this exchange's ANSWER as achira-example (おてあらいはあちらです) but never carded the question, leaving an orphaned answer. The unit quiz (Quiz 1, part II.2) asks the learner to produce exactly this sentence.

items.english: Where is that wine from?
items.target: そのワインはどこのですか
items.pronunciation: sono wain wa doko no desu ka
items.reviewNote: From the TARGET DIALOGUE (verbatim). Distinct from the existing fib-c5-coffee-cup-origin-q, which keeps the noun after どこの; this is the noun-dropped form the dialogue actually uses and nothing in the deck teaches it.
items.note: どこの (doko no) usually has a noun after it — それはどこのコーヒーカップですか (sore wa doko no kōhī kappu desu ka). Here the noun is dropped because ワイン (wain) is already the topic, so どこの is left dangling and means 'from where'.

items.english: This is my bag.
items.target: これはわたしのかばんです
items.pronunciation: kore wa watashi no kaban desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job for の. GRAMMAR 4 introduces a second, quite different job for の (where a thing was made) and the deck never sets it against the ownership の from Lesson 2 — this card and kore-wa-igirisu-no-kaban differ by one word so the contrast is unmissable.
items.note: Half of a minimal pair. Here の (no) says who owns it.

items.english: It's that blue T-shirt over there.
items.target: あのあおいTシャツです
items.pronunciation: ano aoi tīshatsu desu
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 (verbatim), paired with dore-desu-ka. Distinct from KS3 (あのあおいTシャツは3,000えんです), which states a price rather than identifying the item — this is how you point something out when asked.

items.english: Where is this beer from?
items.target: これはどこのビールですか
items.pronunciation: kore wa doko no bīru desu ka
items.reviewNote: From EXERCISES 4B, the worked example (verbatim). Second example of どこの + noun (the first is the existing fib-c5-coffee-cup-origin-q with それ), which keeps that pattern at the two-example cap while contrasting これ against それ. I left its answer (ちゅうごくのです) out on purpose — the deck would then have three 'It's from X' answers.

items.english: Which one is it?
items.target: どれですか
items.pronunciation: dore desu ka
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 1 (verbatim) — the shopkeeper's line. The deck has どれ as vocabulary and a constructed dore-example, but not the bare question a shop assistant actually says to you.
items.note: どれ (dore) is for three or more things. For a choice between two, use どちら (dochira), from Lesson 1.

items.english: Five red apples, please.
items.target: あかいりんごをいつつください
items.pronunciation: akai ringo o itsutsu kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for りんご, which had no sentence anywhere, and stacks GRAMMAR 3 (adjective before noun) onto the counted-request pattern — the deck had those two points only in separate cards.

items.english: How much is it?
items.target: いくらですか
items.pronunciation: ikura desu ka
items.reviewNote: Duplicate of ikura-desu-ka in Lesson 4, the lesson that teaches いくら (ikura). Its answer card carries a hint and stands alone.
items.note: The topic is dropped once it is obvious what you are pointing at. Name the item and it becomes そのワインはいくらですか (sono wain wa ikura desu ka).

items.english: It's from France.
items.target: フランスのです
items.pronunciation: furansu no desu
items.reviewNote: From the TARGET DIALOGUE (verbatim), paired with sono-wain-doko-no. Same shape as the existing fib-c5-coffee-cup-origin-a (イギリスのです, 'It's from England.') but a different gloss, so no English collision; both carry a hint naming their question.
items.scene: answering where the wine is from

items.english: Two glasses and three plates, please.
items.target: コップをふたつとおさらを３まいください
items.pronunciation: koppu o futatsu to osara o san-mai kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job for と — wave 1's cheesecake order was its only sentence — and the VOCABULARY job for both コップ and (お)さら. Unlike the cheesecake order this one mixes two DIFFERENT counters, which is the harder half of the pattern.
items.note: Each item keeps its own を (o) and its own counter; ください (kudasai) is said once at the end. Glasses are round so they take つ (tsu), plates are flat so they take まい (mai).
items.ttsText: コップをふたつとおさらをさんまいください

items.english: Where is that camera over there from?
items.target: あのカメラはどこのですか
items.pronunciation: ano kamera wa doko no desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job — closes the demonstrative ladder and swaps the country for どこの, so the learner sees that the question is the statement with one slot emptied.
items.note: Member 3 of the この (kono) / その (sono) / あの (ano) set, and the one in question form. あの is the thing away from both of you.

items.english: Is that white plate also 1,000 yen?
items.target: そのしろいさらも1,000えんですか
items.pronunciation: sono shiroi sara mo sen'en desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed, following the EXERCISES 5 pattern with different goods so it does not repeat wave 1's black bag. Serves the PARTICLE job for も and the VOCABULARY job for (お)さら and しろい.
items.note: も (mo) takes は (wa)'s place — the two never sit side by side.
items.ttsText: そのしろいさらもせんえんですか

items.english: These are Italian shoes.
items.target: これはイタリアのくつです
items.pronunciation: kore wa itaria no kutsu desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job and the VOCABULARY job for both くつ and イタリア, neither of which had a sentence. The deck has the three forms scattered over unrelated vocabulary and never on one noun.
items.note: Member 1 of a です (desu) / じゃありません (ja arimasen) / ですか (desu ka) set on one noun.

items.english: Are those Italian shoes?
items.target: それはイタリアのくつですか
items.pronunciation: sore wa itaria no kutsu desu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job as the question rung of the triad.
items.note: Member 3 of the set. か (ka) on the end is the whole of the question; the word order does not change. これ (kore) becomes それ (sore) because you are now asking about the other person's side.

items.english: It's 30,000 yen.
items.target: 30,000えんです
items.pronunciation: sanman'en desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed, paired with ookii-soujiki-wa-ikura. Serves the FORM job — the price-answer form deserves practice at more than one order of magnitude, and まん (man) prices appear nowhere in this lesson's sentences.
items.ttsText: さんまんえんです
items.scene: answering how much the large vacuum cleaner costs

items.english: This camera is a Japanese one.
items.target: このカメラはにほんのです
items.pronunciation: kono kamera wa nihon no desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for カメラ and the FORM job for GRAMMAR 2 — the deck teaches この, その and あの as three unrelated vocabulary cards and never shows them stepping away from the speaker on the same noun.
items.note: Member 1 of a この (kono) / その (sono) / あの (ano) set on one noun. この is the thing at your own hand.

items.english: Is this a Swiss watch?
items.target: これはスイスのとけいですか
items.pronunciation: kore wa suisu no tokei desu ka
items.reviewNote: From EXERCISES 4A, the worked example (verbatim). The whole of Exercise 4 never became cards, and GRAMMAR 4 (placeの noun) has only the KS4 statement in the deck. Reuses とけい from Lesson 2 and puts the stranded スイス card to work.
items.note: A place before の (no) says where a thing was made, so スイスのとけい (suisu no tokei) is a watch made in Switzerland, not a watch belonging to Switzerland.

items.english: Eight of those small glasses over there, please.
items.target: あのちいさいコップをやっつください
items.pronunciation: ano chīsai koppu o yattsu kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for ちいさい, which had no sentence, and is the only counted request in the deck that uses あの — ks5 and the fib cards all use その or それ.

items.english: Mikan oranges are 100 yen too.
items.target: みかんも100えんです
items.pronunciation: mikan mo hyaku-en desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job as the も member of the minimal pair.
items.note: The other half of the pair with りんごは100えんです (ringo wa hyaku-en desu). Swapping は (wa) for も (mo) adds 'as well' and nothing else changes.
items.ttsText: みかんもひゃくえんです

items.english: No, they're on the sixth floor.
items.target: いいえ、６かいです
items.pronunciation: īe, rokkai desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed, paired with kamera-wa-yonkai-desu-ka. Serves the VOCABULARY job for ろっかい. The deck's other bare floor answers (さんがいです, ちかいっかいです) are plain corrections of a どこ question; this one opens with いいえ because it is denying a guess.
items.ttsText: いいえ、ろっかいです
items.scene: answering whether the cameras are on the fourth floor

items.english: Ten mikan oranges, please.
items.target: みかんをとおください
items.pronunciation: mikan o tō kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job: とお exists as a recitation card (counter-tsu-10) and the NOTES section makes a point of it being the end of the series, but no sentence uses it.
items.note: とお (tō) is where the ひとつ (hitotsu) series stops. For eleven and up you switch to じゅういち (jūichi) and hang a counter off it.

items.english: One bottle of that red wine, please.
items.target: そのあかワインを１ぽんください
items.pronunciation: sono akawain o ip-pon kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for あかワイン, which had no sentence, and the FORM job for the ぽん shape of the counter, which likewise had none.
items.note: ほん (hon) hardens to ぽん (pon) after いち (ichi), ろく (roku) and じゅう (jū) — hence いっぽん (ip-pon), ろっぽん (rop-pon), じゅっぽん (jup-pon).
items.ttsText: そのあかワインをいっぽんください

items.english: Yes, that one is also 10,000 yen.
items.target: はい、それも10,000えんです
items.pronunciation: hai, sore mo ichiman'en desu
items.reviewNote: From EXERCISES 5, the worked example (verbatim), paired with kono-kuroi-kaban-mo-ichiman. Worth carding for the この→それ pronoun switch that the exercise instructions single out ('Change the pronoun to fit each item') and that no card in the deck demonstrates.
items.note: The shopper says この (kono) because the bag is beside them; the assistant answers それ (sore) because from where they stand the same bag is near the customer.
items.ttsText: はい、それもいちまんえんです
items.scene: answering whether the black bag costs the same

items.english: The wine shop isn't on the first floor. It's in the first-floor basement.
items.target: ワインショップは１かいじゃありません。ちか１かいです
items.pronunciation: wain shoppu wa ikkai ja arimasen. chika ikkai desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job: GRAMMAR 1 (nounは placeです) has no negative example anywhere in the deck, and this is the exact mix-up the TARGET DIALOGUE turns on — ちか１かい is not １かい.
items.note: Correcting someone runs in two parts: deny with じゃありません (ja arimasen), then give the right answer. ちか (chika) in front of a floor number puts it below ground.
items.ttsText: ワインショップはいっかいじゃありません。ちかいっかいです

items.english: Two of those white T-shirts, please.
items.target: そのしろいTシャツを２まいください
items.pronunciation: sono shiroi tīshatsu o ni-mai kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for しろい, which had no sentence, and instantiates the NOTES section's own definition of まい (mai) — 'thin, flat objects like shirts'.
items.ttsText: そのしろいTシャツをにまいください

items.english: The plates are over there.
items.target: おさらはあちらです
items.pronunciation: osara wa achira desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job for GRAMMAR 1 with a place word instead of a floor number — the deck's only あちら sentence is the restroom line from SPEAKING PRACTICE 3, so the pattern rested on one example.
items.note: あちら (achira) points away from both of you, and is the polite word a shop assistant reaches for.

items.english: This is Australian beef.
items.target: これはオーストラリアのぎゅうにくです
items.pronunciation: kore wa ōsutoraria no gyūniku desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for ぎゅうにく, which EXERCISES 4 introduces and no sentence uses. オーストラリア is from Lesson 1. Food is where the origin pattern matters most in real life, and no food card in the deck used it.

items.english: No, it's 900 yen.
items.target: いいえ、900えんです
items.pronunciation: īe, kyūhyaku-en desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed, paired with shiroi-sara-mo-sen-en-ka. Serves the FORM job: every も question in the deck is answered はい, so the learner has never seen one turned down, and correcting a price is the commonest thing that actually happens in a shop.
items.ttsText: いいえ、きゅうひゃくえんです
items.scene: answering whether the white plate costs the same as the other one

items.english: Right, then two bottles of those, please.
items.target: じゃ、それを２ほんください
items.pronunciation: ja, sore o ni-hon kudasai
items.reviewNote: Lifted verbatim from the TARGET DIALOGUE, which wave 1 left out. Serves the FORM job. Distinct from ks5-two-bottles-wine, which names the wine; the hint on this card marks the difference so the two do not collide on an English prompt.
items.note: じゃ (ja) from Lesson 4 is the 'right then' that closes a decision. Once the item is established you drop its name and point with それ (sore).
items.ttsText: じゃ、それをにほんください
items.scene: the wine is already under discussion, so it is not named

items.english: No, they're German ones.
items.target: いいえ、ドイツのです
items.pronunciation: īe, doitsu no desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed, modelled on the EXERCISES 4A answer pattern. Serves the FORM job as the answer to sore-wa-itaria-no-kutsu-ka. The hint keeps it apart from the Lesson 1 card いいえ、ドイツじんです (īe, doitsu jin desu), which is about a person.
items.scene: answering whether the shoes are Italian

items.english: The shoes are on the second floor.
items.target: くつは２かいです
items.pronunciation: kutsu wa ni-kai desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for にかい, one of four floor counters sitting in the deck as recitation cards with no sentence. Reuses くつ from the Italian-shoes set in a completely different frame.
items.ttsText: くつはにかいです

items.english: Please show me that blue T-shirt.
items.target: そのあおいTシャツをみせてください
items.pronunciation: sono aoi tīshatsu o misete kudasai
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job for を in a non-counting frame — every other を card in this lesson ends in a number plus ください. みせてください has been a bare vocabulary card since Lesson 4 with no sentence anywhere in the deck.
items.note: みせてください (misete kudasai) from Lesson 4 asks to be shown something; ください (kudasai) on its own asks to be given it.

items.english: This large glass is 800 yen.
items.target: このおおきいコップは800えんです
items.pronunciation: kono ōkii koppu wa happyaku-en desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job for GRAMMAR 2 and 3 together. KS2 and KS3 price two different shirts with two different pointers, so nothing isolates what actually changed; this pair does.
items.note: Half of a minimal pair with そのちいさいコップは500えんです (sono chīsai koppu wa gohyaku-en desu) — same noun, opposite adjective, opposite pointer.
items.ttsText: このおおきいコップははっぴゃくえんです

items.english: The cheese and the wine are French.
items.target: チーズとワインはフランスのです
items.pronunciation: chīzu to wain wa furansu no desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the PARTICLE job for と in a slot nothing else in the deck uses — every other と card joins two things being ordered with を. Also the VOCABULARY job for チーズ, which had no sentence.
items.note: と (to) glues two nouns into a single topic, so one は (wa) and one です (desu) cover both.

items.english: That small glass is 500 yen.
items.target: そのちいさいコップは500えんです
items.pronunciation: sono chīsai koppu wa gohyaku-en desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the FORM job as the second member of the この/その + おおきい/ちいさい minimal pair.
items.note: The other half of the pair with このおおきいコップは800えんです (kono ōkii koppu wa happyaku-en desu).
items.ttsText: そのちいさいコップはごひゃくえんです

items.english: The information desk is on the first floor.
items.target: インフォメーションは１かいです
items.pronunciation: infomēshon wa ikkai desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Serves the VOCABULARY job for インフォメーション and １かい — the information desk is in the TARGET DIALOGUE's cast and had no sentence, and いっかい only ever appeared bolted onto ちか. States a floor rather than asking for one, so it does not add to the deck's five 〜はどこですか cards.
items.note: １かい is いっかい (ikkai), not いちかい. The same clipping happens at ろっかい (rokkai) and じゅっかい (jukkai).
items.ttsText: インフォメーションはいっかいです
